hero.eyebrow: Stablecoin checkout for independent hotels · Tbilisi pilot
hero.title: Get paid 24 hours after check-in.
hero.titleAccent: Set cancellation terms that fit each guest.
hero.lead: Guests pay in USDC into an escrow that holds your terms. You receive the money in your own wallet 24 hours after they check in, and each guest's cancellation terms are priced for that request.
hero.caveat: Unless the guest opens a dispute in those 24 hours. Disputes are decided by Stumari's arbiter, which during the pilot is a single Stumari key.

problems.title: Three ways independent hotels lose money today

items.title: OTA commission on every booking
items.body: Big booking sites take 15–25% base commission, more with visibility boosters, and pay out weeks later.

items.title: of ordinary bookings cancel, all under one policy
items.body: A family booking six months ahead and a speculative booking two days out get the same blanket terms, so you either lose guests or carry the risk.
items.source: 37% overall, including no-shows and group blocks (Hotel Booking Demand, 119,390 bookings)

items.title: visitors from Russia in 2025
items.body: Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards do not work abroad, so many of these guests already pay small hotels in USDT or USDC informally — straight to an owner's personal wallet, with no receipt and no refund rule. Stripe has never supported Georgia.

steps.title: Connect in one call
steps.body: On a free 20-minute call we connect your Booking.com and Airbnb calendars over iCal where available, set your room rates and choose the contracts you want to offer.

steps.title: Guests choose their terms
steps.body: Your booking link shows each guest a short menu (Flexible, Standard, Non-refundable), each priced for their request. They pay in USDC from a wallet such as Phantom. AI agents can book the same way.

steps.title: Get paid after check-in
steps.body: USDC reaches your wallet 24 hours after check-in. If a guest cancels earlier, the escrow refunds them by their schedule and pays you the rest in the same step.

model.title: The model writes the contract
model.lead: Most hotels have one cancellation policy for everyone. Stumari's model estimates how likely each request is to be cancelled, and when, then prices every contract to target the same expected revenue from this guest as your current policy.
points: Your current policy always costs your normal rate.
A more generous contract costs more, by this guest's estimated risk. A stricter one costs less.
You choose which contracts to offer and the price bounds.

trust.title: Where the money sits
trust.lead: Nobody has to hold the guest's money on trust.

items.title: One escrow per booking
items.body: The guest's USDC goes into an escrow on Solana created for that booking alone. It can pay out only to the guest, to your wallet, or a fee capped by the rate written into the booking.

items.title: Terms fixed before payment
items.body: Price, refund schedule, check-in time and fee are written into the escrow before the guest pays. After that, the program's rules don't let you, the guest or Stumari change them. During the pilot Stumari can still upgrade the program itself: see “What we don't claim”.

items.title: A disclosed arbiter
items.body: If a guest opens a dispute in the 24 hours after check-in, Stumari's arbiter decides how the escrow is split. During the pilot the arbiter is a single Stumari key. We say so openly, and moving to a multi-signature group is on our roadmap.

items.title: Unconfirmed means refunded
items.body: Each booking stays pending until we re-check your calendars. If it isn't confirmed within 2 hours, the guest can take a full refund, so a double booking never costs the guest their money.

limits.title: What we don't claim
limits.body: During the pilot, Stumari can still upgrade the escrow program; it moves to a multi-signature group or is frozen before it holds meaningful funds. Disputed bookings depend on Stumari's arbiter key.

pilot.title: Founding-hotel pilot
pilot.lead: The exact terms, with nothing hidden in the small print.
terms: Founding-hotel pilot for the first 10 independent hotels in Tbilisi.
0% Stumari fee on every booking until 31 December 2026. After that, a flat 1.5% of what the hotel receives, written into each booking on-chain before the guest pays.
Paid in USDC on Solana to a wallet you control, automatically 24 hours after the guest checks in — unless the guest opens a dispute in that window, which Stumari's arbiter decides.
Guest refunds follow the contract the guest chose, automatically.
Guests need only USDC — no SOL, no network fees. Guests holding USDT swap to USDC inside Phantom.
Free 20-minute setup call: we connect your Booking.com/Airbnb calendars (iCal) where available and set your room rates and the contracts you want to offer.
You keep all your existing channels. Stumari adds a direct booking link for guests who pay in stablecoins, and a channel AI agents can book through. We don't bring you guests.
You choose which contracts to offer and your price bounds; the model prices each request to target your current expected revenue.
Per-booking limit of 1,500 USDC during the pilot.
No exclusivity, no minimums, leave anytime.
We help you set up a wallet and point you to licensed providers for converting USDC to lari. We don't give legal, tax or financial advice.

items.a: Payouts arrive as USDC in a wallet you control. To convert USDC to lari, use a licensed provider. We'll point you to options on the setup call. We don't convert funds for you, and this is not financial advice.

items.q: Is it legal for my hotel to accept USDC?
items.a: Ask your accountant. How you accept and declare stablecoin income depends on how your business is registered. We don't give legal, tax or financial advice.

items.q: What if the room is booked on Booking.com at the same moment?
items.a: Every Stumari booking starts as pending. We re-check your calendars before confirming it. If it can't be confirmed within 2 hours, the guest gets a full refund. Confirmed bookings appear in the calendar feed you paste into Booking.com and Airbnb, so the dates close there too.

items.q: What happens if a guest disputes?
items.a: A guest can open a dispute only in the 24 hours after check-in. The payout then waits for Stumari's arbiter, who can split the escrow between the guest and you. During the pilot the arbiter is a single Stumari key. Outside that window the program's rules let nobody redirect the money. During the pilot Stumari can still upgrade the program itself: see “What we don't claim”.
Only USDC on Solana in a wallet such as Phantom. No SOL and no network fees: Stumari pays them. Guests holding USDT swap to USDC inside Phantom first.

items.q: I sell several identical rooms as one room type. Does the calendar sync work?
items.a: Booking.com and Airbnb usually export one iCal calendar per listing, so identical rooms sold as one room type may share a single calendar. We check your extranet together on the setup call before connecting anything. Rooms that are their own listing connect in minutes.
No. We're not an OTA and you keep all your channels. Stumari adds a booking link for guests who pay in stablecoins, and a channel AI agents can book through.
